question: An engineer must configure Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches for Cisco UCS Director integration. The configuration must enable automated onboarding of the switches as they come online. For security purposes, the switches must have the bare minimum of connection methods enabled. The connection protocol must allow authentication through credentials. Which protocol must be configured on the switches to allow automated onboarding?
theory: UCS Director onboards Nexus switches over SSH, which supports credential-based (username/password or key) authentication while keeping the enabled connection surface minimal — satisfying both the 'bare minimum of connection methods' and 'authentication through credentials' requirements. Telnet is unencrypted and inappropriate here, SNMP alone doesn't provide the same interactive, credential-authenticated configuration channel, and HTTPS would additionally require NX-API to be enabled on the switches rather than being the baseline onboarding protocol UCS Director uses for Nexus devices. (Cisco documentation / web research)
